title: Add/Replace/Remove the Johnson transformation type and parameters for a variable
label2: Select a variable to add/replace/remove the Johnson transformation type and parameters (γ, η, ε, λ) where a Johnson transformation was applied previously
selectAddParamsRad: Option 1: Add/Replace the Johnson transformation type and parameters
selectRemoveParamsRad: Option 2: Remove the Johnson transformation type and parameters if they were mistakenly added to the variable
lambda: Lambda (λ) - must be greater than 0 for SB and SU. May be left blank for SL (not used, defaults to 1)
zvalue: (Optional) Z value of the fit - informational only, shown by the Inspect dialog

help.title: Add/Replace/Remove the Johnson transformation type and parameters
help.body:
Description
This dialog is provided for convenience if the Johnson transformation type (SB, SL, or SU) and the parameters Gamma (γ), Eta (η), Epsilon (ε), Lambda (λ) associated with a variable need to be recorded, corrected, or removed. The correct type and parameters are important as they will be used if an inverse Johnson transformation is needed

Typical uses: re-attaching the parameters after they were lost (e.g. the dataset was exported to a file format that does not preserve R attributes and imported back), or recording a Johnson transformation that was performed outside BlueSky Statistics - for example in Minitab, whose Johnson transformation output reports exactly these parameters in its transformation function

The three Johnson transformation functions
SB (bounded): γ + η * Ln( (X - ε) / (λ + ε - X) )
SL (lognormal): γ + η * Ln( X - ε )
SU (unbounded): γ + η * Asinh( (X - ε) / λ )

For reference, Minitab prints the SB function with the upper bound written out, e.g. 0.8046 + 0.8937 * Ln( ( X - 46.2931 ) / ( 59.8636 - X ) ) - there the second constant inside the Ln is λ + ε, so λ = 59.8636 - 46.2931 = 13.5706

Removing always clears the type and all the parameters together, since a partial parameter set cannot be used for the inverse transformation
